title: LLM4DyG: Can Large Language Models Solve Spatial-Temporal Problems on Dynamic Graphs?

problem.claim: The paper addresses whether LLMs can understand spatial-temporal information on dynamic graphs.

gap.claim: LLMs' competence in understanding spatial-temporal information on dynamic graphs remains unexplored in the literature.

contributions.claim: The authors propose the LLM4DyG benchmark with nine tasks evaluating LLM capabilities across temporal and spatial dimensions.
The authors conduct experiments examining the effects of data generators, data statistics, prompting techniques, and LLM choices on performance.
The authors propose Disentangled Spatial-Temporal Thoughts (DST2) to enhance LLMs' spatial-temporal understanding on dynamic graphs.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their evaluation of LLMs' spatial-temporal understanding abilities on dynamic graphs is, to their knowledge, the first.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that LLMs have preliminary spatial-temporal understanding abilities on dynamic graphs.
The authors report that larger and denser graph tasks are more difficult for LLMs, while difficulty is not sensitive to time span or data generation mechanism.
The authors report that DST2 improves spatial-temporal understanding for most tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs are increasingly being explored for handling web and graph data, while dynamic graphs represent temporal network evolution in real-world web data.
Evaluation of LLM spatial-temporal understanding on dynamic graphs is identified as necessary but unexplored.
The paper proposes a first evaluation effort and introduces the nine-task LLM4DyG benchmark.
Experiments study factors affecting performance, followed by the DST2 prompting method.
The authors report preliminary abilities, graph-size and density effects, limited sensitivity to time span and generation mechanism, and improvements from DST2 on most tasks.

source_observation.claim: Task difficulty increases with graph size and density.

interpretation.claim: Graph scale and connectivity density may be important stress dimensions when evaluating LLM reasoning over dynamic graphs.

application.claim: Include graph size and density as controlled evaluation variables for dynamic-graph LLM systems.

exception.claim: The reported difficulty was not sensitive to time span or data generation mechanism.

source_observation.claim: DST2 improves spatial-temporal understanding for most tasks.

interpretation.claim: Separating spatial and temporal reasoning in prompts may help LLMs process dynamic-graph problems.

application.claim: Use disentangled spatial-temporal prompting as a candidate intervention when improving dynamic-graph LLM performance.

exception.claim: The reported improvement applies to most tasks rather than every task.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the nine benchmark task definitions.
The abstract does not provide datasets, model names, quantitative results, or experimental settings.
